entries.meaning: May glorious Śaṅkara protect me: at his left shines the mountain's daughter, the heavenly river rests on his head, a young moon is on his brow, poison is at his throat, and the serpent-king is upon his breast. Adorned with sacred ash, he is the foremost god, lord of all, Śarva, all-pervading, auspicious and moonlike.
entries.note: Original close English rendering from the pinned Devanagari witness; editorial work awaiting independent review.

entries.meaning: May the splendour of Raghunandana's lotus-face—which neither brightened at the prospect of coronation nor withered from the sorrow of forest exile—always bestow lovely auspiciousness upon me.
entries.note: Original close English rendering from the pinned Devanagari witness; editorial work awaiting independent review.

words: attain from the coronation, and likewise

entries.meaning: I bow to Rāma, lord of Raghu's lineage: his tender limbs are dark as a blue lotus, Sītā is seated upon his left side, and in his hand are a mighty arrow and a lovely bow.
entries.note: Original close English rendering from the pinned Devanagari witness; editorial work awaiting independent review.

entries.meaning: Having polished the mirror of my own mind with the dust of the revered guru's lotus feet, I describe Raghuvara's stainless glory, which bestows the four fruits of life.
entries.note: Original close English rendering of the pinned Awadhi reading; editorial work awaiting independent review.
